newsitem.title: UK: McKechnie optimistic despite strong pound.
newsitem.headline: McKechnie optimistic despite strong pound.

text.p: British engineering plastics and metal components group McKechnie Plc said on Wednesday that trading in the second half had started well and satisfactory progress was expected for the full year despite strong sterling affecting overseas earnings.

"The significant strengthening of sterling is affecting the translation of overseas earnings and export margins, but the British construction and DIY markets, which account for 17 percent of our sales, are showing signs of recovery," McKechnie said in a statement.

"With continental Europe past its worst, the U.S. economy stable and the group's usual seasonal bias towards the second half of the year, we look forward to further satisfactory progress," the company added.

The company said the stronger pound had only a marginal impact on the first half. But it warned that if sterling stayed at current rates, the translation of overseas earnings was likely to cost more than 2.0 million stg for the year.
McKechnie said earlier that first-half pretax profits rose 36 percent. It warned it would incur a one off cost of not more than $6.5 million this year to terminate a major loss-making contract.
